findings.note: RFC 2046 5.1.1: only the CRLF immediately before a boundary delimiter belongs to the delimiter. MIMEParser.splitParts trimmed every trailing CR/LF of a part, truncating text attachments and blank lines at the end of a body part.

RFC 2046 5.1.1: a body part may have no header fields, so it starts with the blank line. RFC822Parser looked for the next blank line instead, treating the part's first paragraph as headers and dropping it (the RFC's own sample message lost its first part).
RFC 2046 5.1.5: in multipart/digest a part without Content-Type is message/rfc822, not text/plain. MIMEParser read the digested messages as body text.
RFC 2231 applies to every MIME parameter. MIMEParser only resolved the extended forms of name and filename, so boundary*= (and charset*=) were ignored and the multipart came out empty.
RFC 5322 3.2.2: a comment may contain a quoted-pair. AddressParser's comment stripper ended the comment at an escaped \), leaking the comment's tail into the display name (RFC 5322 A.5).

RFC 5322 4.4: an obs-route before the addr-spec is ignored, and CFWS may surround the dots and the @ of an obs-local-part / obs-domain (A.6.1, A.6.3). AddressParser kept the route and the whitespace in the address.

RFC 5322 4.5 (obs-optional etc.): obsolete syntax allows WSP between a field name and its colon (A.6.3 'From  :'). Python ends the header section at the first such line and reads the rest as the body; SendmailCore parses the fields.

RFC 2045 6.8 / RFC 2047 4.1 require padded base64. Python repairs unpadded or junk input (adds padding, drops bad characters); SendmailCore leaves an undecodable encoded-word literal (RFC 2047 6.3 allows this) and passes an undecodable body through raw.

RFC 5322 2.1 requires an empty line between the header section and the body. Python treats the first line that is not a header field as the start of the body; SendmailCore keeps reading header fields to the first empty line and drops lines without a colon. Input is invalid either way.

RFC 5322 3.4 separates addresses (groups included) with commas, so 'A:a@x;B:b@y;' is invalid. SendmailCore recovers every member; Python returns an empty '<>' mailbox for whatever follows the first group.

':' is a special and must be quoted in a local-part, so 'Carol <b:c@y.test>' is invalid. SendmailCore keeps the angle-addr verbatim (AddressParser.colon_inside_angle_brackets_is_not_a_group); Python splits it into 'b' and '<>'.
'From: MAILER DAEMON' has no addr-spec and is invalid. SendmailCore takes the text as the address; Python takes it as a display name with an empty address. Neither is right; nothing to fix.

With both filename= and filename*= present, SendmailCore prefers the RFC 2231 extended value, as RFC 6266 4.3 recommends for the same parameter pair; Python returns the first one (the ASCII fallback 'ete.pdf').

RFC 2045 5.2 defaults a missing charset to us-ascii; Python decodes 8-bit bytes in such a body to U+FFFD. SendmailCore defaults to utf-8 (a superset of us-ascii) so scripts piping UTF-8 text without MIME headers keep their text.
